column3: In Taiwan this is the standard word for a small rental unit with its own bathroom, typical for students and young workers; a room that shares a bathroom is 雅房. On the mainland it more often means a suite of rooms.
column4: 我在台北租了一间套房。
column5: 我在台北租了一間套房。
column6: Wǒ zài Táiběi zū le yī jiān tàofáng.
column7: I rented a small apartment with its own bathroom in Taipei.
column9: In Taiwan this is the standard word for a small rental unit with its own bathroom, typical for students and young workers; a room that shares a bathroom is 雅房. On the mainland it more often means a suite of rooms.

column6: Zhè ge zì de yīn wǒ bù huì niàn.

column3: As a place name it is Tamsui, the district of New Taipei at the end of the red MRT line, known for its waterfront and old street. As a plain word it is the opposite of 海水, sea water, as in 淡水鱼.
column4: 这条河里有很多淡水鱼。
column5: 這條河裡有很多淡水魚。
column6: Zhè tiáo hé lǐ yǒu hěn duō dànshuǐ yú.

column4: 这个国家大部分的电来自水力发电。

column7: Most of this country's electricity comes from hydroelectric power.

column3: Describes a respectful, deferential manner toward elders or superiors. With 地 it modifies a verb: 恭敬地鞠躬 is to bow respectfully.
column6: Tā gōngjìng de xiàng lǎoshī jūgōng.
column7: He bowed respectfully to the teacher.
column9: Describes a respectful, deferential manner toward elders or superiors. With 地 it modifies a verb: 恭敬地鞠躬 is to bow respectfully.

column3: Describes someone talking: the words are swallowed and spat out by turns, so they come slowly and unclearly, usually because the speaker is embarrassed or hiding something. It goes with 说话.
column4: 他说话吞吞吐吐，好像有什么事瞒着我们。
column5: 他說話吞吞吐吐，好像有什麼事瞞著我們。
column6: Tā shuōhuà tūntūntǔtǔ, hǎoxiàng yǒu shénme shì mán zhe wǒmen.
column7: He talks haltingly, as if he were hiding something from us.
column9: Describes someone talking: the words are swallowed and spat out by turns, so they come slowly and unclearly, usually because the speaker is embarrassed or hiding something. It goes with 說話.
